entities.summary: Thomas Michael Kettle was an Irish economist, journalist, barrister, writer, war poet, soldier and Home Rule politician. As a member of the Irish Parliamentary Party, he was Member of Parliament (MP) for East Tyrone from 1906 to 1910 at Westminster. He joined the Irish Volunteers in 1913, then on the outbreak of World War I in 1914 enlisted for service in the British Army, with which he was killed in action on the Western Front in the autumn of 1916. He was a much admired old comrade of James Joyce, who considered him to be his best friend in Ireland, as well as the likes of Francis Sheehy-Skeffington, Oliver St.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a Home Rule politician and soldier, Tom Kettle's actions contributed to his death in action on the Western Front during World War I, resulting in the loss of a prominent Irish voice in the lead-up to independence. His legacy as a war poet and writer also left a lasting impact on Irish literature.
